voyage.content: New York-style pizza that rivals anything you could find in New York city. Delancey is the product of NY transplants and its attention to detail shows. The menu is simple and well executed, basically just pizza and salad.

voyage.name: Ridge Pizza
voyage.content: Neighborhood pizza joint. Pizza varieties named after local shops and restaurants.

voyage.name: Old Salt
voyage.content: House-made bagels with in-house smoked fish.

voyage.name: Rachel's Bagels & Burritos
voyage.content: House-made bagels, biscuits, and burritos.

voyage.name: The Walrus and The Carpenter
voyage.content: Excellent oyster bar in a restored historic building. No reservations; the wait is often 1-2 hours unless you get there very early. The adjacent Barnacle bar is a great place to wait while sipping Italian aperitif cocktails and antipasti.

voyage.name: Rupee Bar
voyage.content: Intimate bar presenting modern cocktails & small plates inspired by Sri Lanka & India.

voyage.name: Copine
voyage.content: Classic French technique meets local ingredients in a breezy, sophisticated space. Menu is typically prixe fixe only, with bar seating with a smaller menu.

voyage.name: Ray's Boathouse and Ray's Cafe
voyage.content: Great views and, in the downstairs Boathouse restaurant, some of the best seafood cooking in the city, priced accordingly. Upstairs, Ray's Cafe is more casual, the food is good but not comparable to the Boathouse downstairs.

voyage.name: Jolly Roger/Maritime Pacific Brewing Company
voyage.content: The Jolly Roger serves as the taproom for Maritime Pacific Brewing Company, the oldest brewery in Ballard, with upscale pub food, in-house beers & pirate-themed decor.

voyage.name: Fair Isle Brewing
voyage.content: Brewery and taproom specializing in lagers and mixed-culture saisons using farmed and foraged ingredients such as fireweed, raspberries, elderberries, madrone bark, etc. The brewery also has a restaurant with snacks, small plates, and mains with vegetarian, seafood, and meat options.

voyage.name: Angry Beaver
voyage.content: Said to be the only Canadian-themed bar in Seattle. Great poutine, perfect for hockey fanatics. Full bar.

voyage.name: Prost!
voyage.price: $5-6 for half a liter, $10-12 for a liter of beer
voyage.content: Great little Bavarian-style German pub loaded with great German beer and all beers served in their appropriate glassware.

voyage.name: Bleacher's
voyage.content: Standard sports bar, stiff drinks.

voyage.name: Gainsbourg
voyage.content: French fare with great variety of wine, beer, cocktails, and absinthe.

voyage.name: The Baranof
voyage.content: Classic dive. A Greenwood institution. Go for the karaoke.

voyage.name: Little Tin
voyage.content: Cocktail bar with Tiki and Hawaiian-inspired drinks and snacks.

voyage.name: Olaf's
voyage.content: Relaxed neighborhood watering hole featuring a wide selection of draft beers & elevated bar bites. Two televisions usually showing sports.

voyage.name: Old County Bar
voyage.content: Sports bar with full bar, several beers on draft, one pool table and darts. Several televisions usually showing sports.

voyage.name: Miro Tea
voyage.content: A contemporary tea house with a large selection of beverages and food.

voyage.name: Valentinas Cafe
voyage.content: Delicious Mexican-inspired coffee and tea drinks and pastries in a whimsical, floral-themed space.

voyage.name: Victrola Coffee Roasters
voyage.content: Excellent spot to grab a drink, get a little work done, or peoplewatch at the popular corner of Market and 22nd.

voyage.name: Venture Coffee Co
voyage.content: Eco-conscious, counter-serve coffeehouse featuring varied fair-trade blends & light fare.

voyage.name: Hotel Ballard
voyage.content: Mediterranean-style hotel in the heart of Ballard. 29 rooms and suites with marble and carpet tiles in lavish rooms. It also hosts Stoneburner, an in-house pizzeria, in the lobby, and a rooftop pavilion. For pampering or sports, an athletic club with swimming pool, gym, and spa is just next door.

voyage.name: Ballard Inn
voyage.price: From $100 per night for room with a shared bathroom
voyage.content: An updated inn with 16 small rooms, some with shared bathrooms.

voyage.name: Greenlake Guest House
voyage.content: A 4-room bed and breakfast overlooking Green Lake. The couple who own the place cook breakfast and constantly chat with guests.

voyage.name: Fremont Bridge
voyage.content: A bascule bridge (drawbridge) spanning the Fremont Cut since 1917. The bridge opens an average of 35 times a day, which makes it the most frequently opened drawbridge in the United States and one of the busiest bascule bridges in the world.

voyage.name: Gas Works Park
voyage.content: "Gasworks" is Wallingford's oddly endearing refuge along the north part of Lake Union — prominently featuring the rusting, hulking remains of the city's old gasworks piping and machinery. More conventionally, a solitary bump of a hill offers the ideal spot for kite flying and views across the lake of sailboats, float planes landing, and downtown Seattle at sunset. Generally quiet but exceptionally crowded during the

voyage.name: Woodland Park
voyage.content: One of the city's most active hubs for sports and recreation, including walkway paths, several playfields, tennis courts, lawn bowling, horseshoe pits, a skatepark, and a large, wooded dog off-leash area.

voyage.name: Woodland Park Zoo
voyage.price: May–September $18.75 per adult, $11.75 per child; October–May $11.75 per adult, $8.75 per child. Discounts for using public transit or on a rainy day!
voyage.content: The zoo hosts 1,100 animals from 300 different species, each housed in nice, naturalistic exhibits. You can feed a giraffe or an elephant by yourself for $5, or enter the aviary where the birds fly overhead and show off talents with the aid of a zookeeper. For the kids, the zoomazium is an additional place to visit for slides and a century-old carousel. Allow at least 3 hours of your time to fully explore the zoo.

voyage.name: Waiting for the Interurban
voyage.address: N. 34th St. at Fremont Ave., at the north approach to the Fremont Bridge
voyage.content: A statue of five people (and a dog) waiting for the trolley that has not existed since the 1930s. The statue is frequently clothed by local residents. There was a time when this work was considered offbeat (imagine that!).

voyage.name: Fremont Rocket
voyage.content: A 53' Cold War rocket, improved with neon space blasters and a smoke generator in the engine bay, towers over the corner of N. 35th Street and Evanston Avenue.

voyage.name: Fremont Troll
voyage.content: Strikingly large (photos generally don't do it justice), the Troll is a concrete statue under the Aurora Bridge clutching a full size Volkswagen Bug in its grip. The statue is notable enough to even gets its own street name - just off of N. 36th Street on Troll Avenue.

voyage.name: Statue of Lenin
voyage.content: This bronze statue peers out over the street below, oblivious to the continuing controversy over its display. It was salvaged and brought over from Slovakia and was re-erected in 1995 in a Fremont parking lot that at the time hosted a weekly market before being moved a few years later to its current site.

voyage.name: Tai Chi at Meridian Park
voyage.content: On most Sunday mornings, groups of people practice tai chi or assorted other martial arts in the southeast quadrant of Meridian Park.

voyage.name: Fremont Abbey Arts Center
voyage.content: A performing and demonstrative arts venue.

voyage.name: Fremont Fair
voyage.content: If you happen to be in Seattle around the Summer Solstice, Fremont hosts one of the city's best street fairs on the weekend closest to the solstice. The highlight is the Solstice Parade on Saturday afternoon, an arts-only parade held by the Fremont Art's Council with hundreds, perhaps even thousands, of elaborately costumed participants, no signage (strongly discouraging commercial participation), and only human-powe

voyage.name: Fremont Oktoberfest
voyage.price: From $15 if purchased in advance, $20 same day
voyage.content: An annual microbrew tasting event that features the Texas Chainsaw Pumpkin Carving Contest, live music, three beer gardens, a dog day event, the Brew HA-HA 5K, a comedy show, and the Miss Buxom Contest.

voyage.name: Archie McPhee
voyage.content: Novelty store with a variety of gag gifts and odd items, as well as the Rubber Chicken Museum and the Wallingford Beast. Exploring the shop is an experience.

voyage.name: Dusty Strings
voyage.content: Lots of acoustic, and mostly stringed, musical instruments. Go on in and try out a hammer dulcimer. Ask Olivia to try out a harp!

voyage.name: Evo
voyage.content: Popular outdoor gear retailer for skis, snowboards, bikes, mountain bikes, skateboards, longboards, surfboards, outerwear, and men's & women’s clothing. The space includes an art gallery, music venue and movie theater. Offers a variety of bike rentals, with helmets and maps included.

voyage.name: Dick's Drive-In
voyage.content: This is a local legend of a drive-in/drive-out burger joint which has served the dual purpose of providing a gathering place for high school and UW students before and after sporting events.

voyage.name: Paseo Caribbean Restaurant
voyage.content: A tiny Cuban restaurant with amazing sandwiches like a crunchy baguette slathered with a secret aioli and filled with your choice of protein (the most popular is the roasted pork shoulder), fresh cilantro, pickled jalapeños, lettuce and delicious caramelized onions. A local favorite, it's best to call ahead and place your order. Expect to settle for takeout; the 3 tables are usually full but there are several nearby

voyage.name: The Dish
voyage.content: New American cuisine. Home of the Slacker Special: scrambled eggs or tofu, cheese, tortilla chips, enchilada sauce and sour cream served with potatoes and toast. Although you might see a line outside, it never takes long to be seated and it's worth the wait.

voyage.name: Musashi's
voyage.content: A small hole-in-the-wall Japanese eatery that attracts crowds of patrons waiting for a bowl of sushi rice with assorted sashimi (called chirashi), which is not listed on the menu. Opens for lunch and dinner only. Cheap for its portion sizes.

voyage.name: Ivar's Salmon House
voyage.content: Various seafood entrees served in a neo-longhouse replete with totem poles and various other carved cedar adornments. Ivar's has an excellent and affordable happy hour menu (7 days a week 3:30PM-6:30PM and 9PM-close) that many locals and University of Washington staff and faculty enjoy regularly. The thing to get is salmon smoked to order over the big wood fire in the northwest style.

voyage.name: TangleTown Public House
voyage.content: Pub and patio where pizza is popular fare.

voyage.name: George and Dragon
voyage.content: British style pub with pretty standard dark wood interior. Great for watching soccer games.

voyage.name: Murphy's Pub
voyage.content: Irish pub with a good selection of drinks, fair pub food. Attracts a young and educated crowd. Trivia on Tuesday evenings.

voyage.name: Sea Monster Lounge
voyage.content: Decent selection of beer, cocktails, and wine. Fresh sushi made onsite with sake. Free live music every night.

voyage.name: Zoka Coffee
voyage.content: In what is variously known as the Meridian District or Tangletown, between Wallingford and Green Lake. Hip students, professionals, and soccer moms meet here. Great desserts and whole grain scones. Roasts their own coffee, supplying to cafes across the U.S. and at Zoka's two cafes in Japan. There is also one north of the U-Village shopping complex on Blakely.

voyage.name: Fremont Brewing
voyage.content: Local brewery with large outdoor beer garden (Urban Beer Garden) as well as an indoor area. Has a wide area of beer available for pickup as well as dine-in.

voyage.name: Hotel Hotel
voyage.content: European style hotel/hostel in the heart of Fremont.

voyage.name: Carkeek Park
voyage.content: The century-old trees and surprisingly steep terrain surrounding a small valley give the impression that you're far from the city. Excellent for a walk in the woods. Walkable beach below the train tracks.

voyage.name: Maple Leaf Park
voyage.content: This area used to be a reservoir. It is now drained, replaced by a wide open green area locals used for playing, but the water tower is still standing. As it is the highest spot in North Seattle, you can catch a wonderful panorama of downtown Seattle, Mount Rainier, the Cascades, Lake Washington, and partially blocked Olympic Mountains.

voyage.name: Warren G. Magnuson Park
voyage.content: Seattle's second-largest park, formerly the Sand Point Naval Air Station. The wide-open spaces of the park support numerous athletic fields and picnic spots, with windsurfing and a boat launch along the Lake Washington shoreline. The buildings remaining from its military days are home to many community organizations and special events.

voyage.name: Granite Curling Club
voyage.content: An excellent facility dedicated to curling, the loud ice sport with stones and brooms. They host regular open houses to teach people how to play.

voyage.name: Kraken Community Iceplex
voyage.content: This practice facility for the Seattle Kraken hockey team is open for public skate sessions over lunch hours, weekends and evenings.

voyage.name: Jackson Park Golf Course
voyage.price: Championship course: $35 weekday, $45 weekend; Executive course: $8.50 9-hole, $14.00 18-hole (playing twice)
voyage.content: A decent 18-hole championship and a 9-hole executive golf course plus a driving range.

voyage.name: Underwater Sports
voyage.content: You can buy diving gear here but the unique thing about this place is that they offer open water scuba diving certification classes, as well as more basic swimming classes. Lessons conducted at their indoor pool and then out in the Puget Sound.

voyage.name: Lake City Summer Festival and Parade
voyage.address: along NE 125th Street from 25th Avenue NE to Lake City Way NE
voyage.content: Lake City has a great street fair in late summer, complete with street vendors, food, music and a parade with local kids and performers on up to the SeaFair Pirates. It has a small-town feel while the streets are lined with all sorts of families and crazies from the neighborhood. Fun for all.

voyage.name: Northgate Station
voyage.content: A mall that existed since the 1950s, that is now transitioning to a large mixed-used development.

voyage.name: Green Lake Jewelry Works
voyage.content: Custom made jewelry. Rings are especially pricey and takes weeks to make, but made to the utmost precision & worth every penny.

voyage.name: Asian Family Market
voyage.content: A large supermarket with an extensive selection of Chinese and other East Asian produce and ingredients.

voyage.name: Math 'n' Stuff
voyage.content: A toy shop mainly for bookworms & brain teasers, and the artsy.

voyage.name: Burgermaster
voyage.content: Designed to be a drive-thru, but there's limited seating area inside. American style burgers & sandwiches that is not the fast food norm; it is a 60-year-old local family brand that has higher standards. Other items include milkshakes, fish & chips, salads, and snacks.

voyage.name: Family Donut
voyage.content: Very good family-run doughnut shop with excellent donuts and coffee.

voyage.name: Grateful Bread Bakery & Cafe
voyage.content: Grateful Bread is a bakery and cafe that offers handmade bread and pastries, as well as espresso and panini sandwiches. It is predominantly a family spot, especially during the period right before and after school. It is locally owned and has a very casual atmosphere.

voyage.name: Jewel Box Cafe
voyage.content: A quaint and warm cafe under an apartment complex. Bubble tea, coffee and tea with special mixes, sandwiches, breakfast and its house special: crepes.

voyage.name: Pho An
voyage.content: A medium restaurant for a big appetite. Where else would you find pho with oxtail? Humongous & soothing portion of pho, and other accompaniments such as spring roll, fried tofu or banh mi (Vietnamese sandwich).

voyage.name: Taqueria de Pasadita
voyage.content: A food cart that though may not look so crowded (most people have it to-go), but lures regulars for their cheap yet succulent piece of taco and assorted Mexican street grubs. Even they offer traditional drinks such as champurado and horchata.

voyage.name: Chaiyo Thai Cuisine
voyage.hours: Mon-Thu 11AM-9PM, Fri 11AM-10PM, Sat noon-10PM, Sun noon-9PM
voyage.content: Thai dishes from all regions north to south. Try its spicy seafood fried rice and Pad See Ew. You can choose the level of spiciness for your dish.

voyage.name: Enat
voyage.content: The area is home to an Ethiopian & Eritrean church and fellow restaurants. Order the injera or the combos which consists of vegetables and/or meat on top of a big piece of bread, very filling for not 1, but 2 people.

voyage.name: Fiddler's Inn
voyage.content: A cabinlike ambiance, fantastic beer on tap, and an eclectic menu of food ranging from vegetarian burritos to some great pizza.

voyage.name: Kona Kitchen
voyage.content: Hawaiian style diner. All day breakfast, Hawaiian lunch and dinner specials. Savour the mac & cheese, mochiko chicken, kalua pig, spam musubi, or for more meat, Da Kanak Attack (lunch only). Rice portion is small and comes in scoops.

voyage.name: Saffron Grill
voyage.content: A fine establishment providing Indian and Mediterranean food. Same owners and same basic menu Taste of India in the U-District. Happy hour food and drink deals from 2PM to 7PM.

voyage.name: Santorini Pizza & Pasta
voyage.content: Neighborhood Italian (with some Greek tones) restaurant known for good food and house wine. The cooks have a tendency to use ample amounts of cheese. Extremely large dessert portions, particularly the baklava.

voyage.name: Wedgwood Broiler
voyage.content: The Wedgwood Broiler offers two distinct microcosms. The bar/lounge includes a healthy mix of patrons of varying ages and trivia nights while the main restaurant area is a considerably more grim affair with geriatric customers lurking in a gloomy, windowless room. Nevermind the aesthetics though. The food here is excellent, including a French dip with some of the best au jus ever created, and a chicken caesar salad w

voyage.name: Toyoda Sushi
voyage.content: Off-the-wall family-run restaurant specializing in fresh sushi & sashimi. Sit at the bar to see its making and if you aren't picky, ask for whatever they want to make & they will serve you. Specials are spicy tuna bowl and chef's choice. Free appetizer and miso soup.

voyage.name: Boud's Pinehurst Pub
voyage.content: A dive bar with breakfast all day. Competitions every day such as Trivia Monday (except on football season), pool Tuesdays, beer pong Wednesdays. Daily drink specials. Happy hour 2-4PM & 9-11PM.

voyage.name: Elliott Bay Brewing Company
voyage.content: Its name has spoken as a Seattle local brand. 100% organic barley as malt to brew a myriad of recipes. Drinks & gourmet snacks, none else. Monthly pairing specials also available.

voyage.name: The Rickshaw
voyage.content: Best karaoke in town, and a mai tai that will lay you out. Happy hour is noon-6PM.

voyage.name: Tim's Tavern on 105th
voyage.content: Full fledged bar. Open mic every Tuesday & Sunday. And jamming live music every day. Private patio, beer garden, free parking.

voyage.name: Wedgwood Public House
voyage.content: Locally owned, with great beer and delicious, made from scratch pub food.

voyage.name: Cafe Javasti
voyage.content: Gourmet coffee drinks, homemade baked goods, and crepes.

voyage.name: Van Gogh Coffeehouse
voyage.content: Espresso drinks, wine and gelato.

voyage.name: Comfort Inn
voyage.content: Not a sketchy place to stay but rooms look slightly worn out. Breakfast is a grab and go.

voyage.name: Hotel Nexus
voyage.content: Free wi-fi, outdoor pool, complimentary scheduled shuttle service, and free room service from the on-site Indian restaurant, Saffron Grill.
